# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Intake brief — Consolidate and complete the end-to-end "creating a new game" guide

**Work item:** CG-0MUZFNOE1007T57S (`chore`, high)
**Blocks:** CG-0MUZFNCAC008B0KZ (1916: The Rising epic)

## Problem statement

There is no single, complete, end-to-end guide for creating a new TCE example
game. The guidance is split across three places with overlapping, partially
stale content, so a new-game author (human or agent) must reconcile three
documents and can follow retired instructions:

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` → **Adding an Example Game** (line ~1571): repo layout,
  scaffold, `GAME_INFO`, `configs/*.json` preset, transcript/replay, publish —
  accurate but scattered and unlinked from the end-to-end lifecycle.
- `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/SKILL.md` (841 lines): engine/implementation
  conventions, but describes the retired **flat monorepo** (in-tree
  `example-games/<game>/`, "add to the `GAMES` array in `main.ts`"), and
  duplicates ~14 of its 17 sections from the always-loaded `AGENTS.md` and
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — which is why it has drifted.
- `docs/the-build/` (ideation, genre research, engine-capabilities audit,
  concept-evaluation rubric): the canonical pre-intake concept process, **not
  linked** from either of the above.

The gap was confirmed during the 1916: The Rising intake (CG-0MUZFNCAC008B0KZ).

## Users

- **New-game author (primary; human developer or AI agent).** Needs one place
  to read the full lifecycle, from "should this be a game?" to "it is shipped
  and registered", with copy-pasteable commands.
  - *As an author*, I want a single canonical guide so that I don't have to
    reconcile three documents and second-guess which is current.
  - *As an author*, I want the guide to link to the authoritative deep dives
    (multi-repo architecture, SLL, HUD, testing) rather than restate them, so
    it stays correct.
- **AI agent working the worklog (secondary).** Needs a compact, agent-facing
  reference (when-to-use + pitfalls + a definition-of-done checklist) that does
  not duplicate the always-loaded `AGENTS.md` in its context window.
  - *As an agent*, I want a slim `tce-game-dev` skill that points at the guide
    and `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, so I do not load 841 lines of stale, duplicated
    prose.
- **Producer / reviewer (tertiary).** Needs the compliance checklist in one
  authoritative place to review a new game's completeness.

## Existing state

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (4243 lines) has a top-level Table of Contents and a
  §**Adding an Example Game** section (accurate on the multi-repo model, but not
  framed as a lifecycle).
- `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/SKILL.md` (841 lines, tracked in `.pi/skills/`,
  project-local only — no README/doc references it, and `~/.pi/agent/skills` has
  no copy). Its §2 "flat monorepo" model and §2 "add to the `GAMES` array in
  `main.ts`" instruction are stale; §11/§12 assume the pre-split test/CI layout.
- `AGENTS.md` (648 lines, always loaded) already carries 22 "Game Architecture
  Best Practices" patterns plus UI modal-dialog best practices.
- `docs/the-build/` exists but is not linked from `README.md`,
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, or the skill.
- Authoritative multi-repo references already exist:
  `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` (457),
  `docs/dev/game-configuration.md` (341),
  `docs/dev/per-game-src-layout-decision.md` (357).
- No documentation link-checker or docs-consistency test exists.

## Desired change

1. Create a single canonical end-to-end guide at
   `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md`, covering the full lifecycle:
   concept/ideation & engine-capability evaluation (`docs/the-build/`) →
   intake/plan → repo scaffold & multi-repo setup → architecture/implementation
   (SLL, HUD, audio/SFX, reduced motion, persistence, AI) → testing profiles →
   CI/release → registration (`GAME_INFO` + `configs/*.json`) →
   assets/licensing → docs update → publication. The guide **links to** the
   authoritative deep dives instead of restating them.
2. Reduce `docs/DEVELOPER.md` §**Adding an Example Game** to a short pointer at
   the guide (moving, not duplicating, the lifecycle framing), and add a link
   from `README.md`.
3. Slim and correct `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/SKILL.md` to a non-duplicative
   agent-facing reference: keep §1 invocation framing, §16 Common Pitfalls, and
   §17 checklist (the single source of truth); replace the stale/duplicated
   narrative sections with links to the guide and `docs/DEVELOPER.md`; correct
   the multi-repo facts.
4. Add a lightweight docs-consistency test so the guide/skill cannot silently
   drift again.

### Decisions taken during intake

- **Q1 = (a).** A new file `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` is the canonical
  guide; `DEVELOPER.md` §Adding an Example Game becomes a stub; the skill is
  updated and cross-linked.
- **Q2 = (c).** Slim refactor of the skill (non-duplicative, ~150–200 lines),
  not a minimal patch and not a monolithic rewrite.
- **Q3 = (a).** The skill's §17 checklist is the single source of truth; the
  guide links to it and does not duplicate it.

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC1 — Canonical guide.** A single canonical guide exists at
`docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md`, covers every lifecycle stage listed in
"Desired change" with copy-pasteable commands, links to (rather than restates)
the authoritative deep-dive docs, and is reachable from `README.md` and
`docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

**AC2 — De-duplication / single source of truth.** `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
§Adding an Example Game is a short pointer to the guide; the guide, the skill
and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` contain no contradictory instructions (in particular,
no residual "flat monorepo" or `main.ts` `GAMES` array guidance).

**AC3 — Skill slimmed and corrected.** `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/SKILL.md` is a
non-duplicative agent-facing reference (target ~150–200 lines) retaining §1
(when to use), §16 (Common Pitfalls) and §17 (checklist), with its
multi-repo facts corrected (sibling `../tce-<game>` repos + `./core` submodule,
Vite `GAME_INFO` discovery + `configs/*.json` presets, per-game
`CORE_ROOT=./core` scripts).

**AC4 — Optional systems, cross-repo rules and definition of done.** The guide
explicitly references accessibility/reduced motion, Steam
achievements/challenges mapping (optional), runtime-plugin artifacts
(optional), and cross-repo change/push rules (`dev` only, never `main`); and a
"definition of done" checklist is reachable from the top of the guide via a
link to the skill's §17, with no duplicated checklist body.

**AC5 — Verifiable and green.** A unit test exists that asserts the guide file
exists with each required lifecycle section, that every relative link (and
anchor) in the guide resolves, and that neither the guide nor the skill
contains the retired monorepo phrases; all related documentation is updated;
`npm run build` succeeds; and the full project test suite passes with the new
changes.

## Constraints

- **Docs-only chore** — no engine/game behaviour changes; no new runtime code
  beyond the docs-consistency test.
- **Do not duplicate canonical content.** The guide links to
  `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`, `game-configuration.md`,
  `per-game-src-layout-decision.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` deep dives, and the
  skill's §17 checklist.
- **Skill file is agent infrastructure.** It is edited here only because AC3
  explicitly authorises it; changes elsewhere in `.pi/` are out of scope.
- **UK English** in all docs and comments.
- **`dev` only** — never push to `main`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` — **new**; the canonical end-to-end guide.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — reduce §Adding an Example Game to a pointer; add guide
  to the Table of Contents; verify no contradictory instructions remain.
- `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/SKILL.md` — slim refactor + multi-repo correction;
  §17 remains the single authoritative checklist.
- `README.md` — link the guide (documentation index / contributor section).
- `docs/the-build/*` — verify each file is linked from the guide's concept
  phase; adjust only links if needed.
- `tests/tooling/creating-a-new-game-guide.test.ts` (or
  `tests/scripts/…`) — **new** docs-consistency unit test.
- Possibly `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` / `game-configuration.md` —
  add reciprocal links back to the guide.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — drift returns (medium).** A hand-maintained guide can drift like the
  skill did. *Mitigation:* AC5 docs-consistency test + link-don't-restate
  policy.
- **Risk — over-long guide (medium).** Attempting a full lifecycle narrative
  could reproduce the duplication problem in one file. *Mitigation:* explicit
  link-don't-restate constraint; keep the guide a navigation layer.
- **Risk — skill content loss (medium).** Slamming the skill could drop a
  genuinely unique convention. *Mitigation:* before trimming, diff each removed
  section against `AGENTS.md`/`docs/DEVELOPER.md`; relocate any unique content
  into the guide or a deep-dive doc rather than deleting it.
- **Assumption:** the authors of new games are both humans and agents, so the
  guide must be readable and linkable.
- **Assumption:** `docs/the-build/` files are canonical and correct as-is (only
  linkage is in scope).
- **Assumption:** a docs-consistency test is acceptable in the unit suite (fast,
  filesystem-only).
- **Scope-creep:** rewriting `docs/DEVELOPER.md` wholesale, adding a docs-site
  generator, or porting the guide to the sibling game repos is **out of scope**;
  record as linked follow-ups instead.

## Related work

**Curated (manually verified):**

- **CG-0MUZFNCAC008B0KZ** — *1916: The Rising* epic; **blocked-by** this chore
  so the guide is corrected before the new game is implemented.
- **CG-0MM4RHCEL0MEJ8HL / CG-0MM4RAHP40H5OTZI / CG-0MM4RAT5L12FHWKP /
  CG-0MM4RBOUS10PJ64E** — The Build ideation, genre research, engine-capability
  audit and concept-evaluation rubric (the guide's concept/ideation phase).
- **CG-0MS9EJO6L006OTF6 / CG-0MRPH9YF0008QIZY** — authored the `tce-game-dev`
  skill (the artefact this chore refactors).
- **CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17** — multi-repo distribution epic (sibling `tce-<game>` +
  `./core` submodule model; children F1 CG-0MTRO6P18003AZIZ, F5
  CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC, F6 CG-0MTRO7BFQ003IN2X, F9 CG-0MUH0NTRG007GDME).
- **CG-0MUI9K4F8009DYJL** — ALPHA banner/version on all game screens
  (registration/launcher precedent for a new game).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MMLDBB070D8LO7T** – On the second game the Activity Log doesn't show any output (completed)
- **CG-0MUINDD9Q00725QT** – Verify fresh remote clones: game repos and launcher presets (completed)
- **CG-0MP12WI75001L9P4** – Transcript & SaveLoad Consolidation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ac4, ac5, acceptance, accessibility, achievements (+114 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, accessibility, achievements, add, adding (+97 more)
- `README.md` — matched: achievements, add, architecture, artifacts, assets (+74 more)

_(full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-CG-0MUZFNOE1007T57S.md`)_

## Appendix A: Clarifying questions & answers

| # | Question | Answer | Source |
|---|----------|--------|--------|
| Q1 | Deliverable shape / canonical home: (a) new `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` canonical + DEVELOPER.md stub + skill cross-linked; (b) expand DEVELOPER.md in place; (c) retire the skill and fold into DEVELOPER.md. | **(a)** New canonical guide file; DEVELOPER.md §Adding an Example Game becomes a stub; skill updated and cross-linked. | Interactive reply (producer), 2026-10-08. |
| Q2 | How much of the skill to fix: (a) minimal multi-repo facts only; (b) comprehensive fix but keep monolithic; (c) slim non-duplicative refactor (~150–200 lines); (d) retire. | Initial answer "not sure — re-evaluate whether it is useful as a monolithic skill"; after evidence review, **(c)** slim non-duplicative refactor. Research: the skill is 841 lines and duplicates ~14/17 sections already in always-loaded `AGENTS.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, which is why it drifted (flat-monorepo/§2, `main.ts` `GAMES` array, pre-split §11/§12); it is project-local only and unreferenced. Unique value: §1 when-to-use, §16 pitfalls, §17 checklist. | Interactive reply (producer) + repo analysis, 2026-10-08. |
| Q3 | Definition-of-done checklist ownership: (a) skill §17 is the single source of truth, guide links to it; (b) duplicate a checklist in the guide and keep in sync manually. | **(a)** Skill §17 is the single source of truth; the guide links to it. | Interactive reply (producer), 2026-10-08. |

## Goal

Add a pure, framework-free DLC gate helper that any game uses to gate content on the unified unlock state, and prove it end-to-end with a Gym scene whose content is unreachable until the action is verified. Proof target: Gym scene only (producer decision); per-game roll-out is follow-up work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pure helper (`src/core-engine/DlcGate.ts` or equivalent) gates content on `isUnlocked({ kind: 'dlc', gameId, dlcId })`.
- An unknown, unreadable, or absent unlock state degrades to "not unlocked" and never crashes the owning game.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymDlcUnlockScene.ts` demonstrates a DLC content item that is locked until verified, then reachable, with a documented locked-state presentation.
- A unit test covers the gate helper; a browser/Gym test covers the gated-content UI (locked → verified → reachable); tests pass under their projects.

## Minimal Implementation

- New pure `src/core-engine/DlcGate.ts` (no Phaser/Electron dependency; takes an unlock-check function).
- New Gym scene using SLL and the existing Gym scene base, consuming the F5 read client.
- Locked-state presentation documented in the scene help text.

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/DlcGate.ts` — **new**: pure DLC unlock gate.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymDlcUnlockScene.ts` — **new**: proof scene.
- `tests/core-engine/DlcGate.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/gym/GymDlcUnlock.browser.test.ts` — **new**.

## Deliverables

Gate helper + Gym proof scene + unit/browser tests.

## Dependencies

- Generalised IPC/preload bridge and total read API (F5).

## Test Plan

`npx vitest run --project unit tests/core-engine/DlcGate.test.ts` and `npx vitest run --project browser tests/gym/GymDlcUnlock.browser.test.ts`

# Docs-consistency guard test for the "creating a new game" guide

Discovered-from: CG-0MUZFNOE1007T57S. Test-first guard for the canonical
end-to-end new-game guide consolidation. This item defines the contract that
F2 (guide) and F4 (skill) must satisfy.

## Goal

As a docs maintainer, I want a fast filesystem-only unit test that pins the
guide's required lifecycle sections, resolves every relative link and in-file
anchor, and rejects the retired monorepo phrases — so the guide and skill
cannot silently drift again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit test exists at `tests/tooling/creating-a-new-game-guide.test.ts` and runs under `--project unit` (the `unit` project includes `tests/**/*.test.ts`).

## Goal

As a new-game author (human or agent), I want one canonical guide covering the
full lifecycle — from "should this be a game?" to "it is shipped and

| F5 | Verify guide consolidation and run release gates (CG-0MUZRA51W001GAYU) | task | high | F2, F3, F4 | build + unit + full-suite gate evidence |

Each content feature is a complete slice (content + the F1 guard that pins it +
links). F1 is the tracer-bullet test written first (red), F2 makes the guide
green, F3 and F4 complete the de-duplication/skill slices, and F5 is the
integration gate. Before each phase starts, its item description is reviewed
and updated against the then-current state.

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — every child AC traces to a parent AC; F1→AC5 (test), F2→AC1/AC4, F3→AC1(reachability)/AC2, F4→AC3, F5→AC5(build/suite). No invented ACs.

5. **Acceptance & testability** — all ACs are pass/fail and checkable (test assertions, grep checks, build/test exit codes).
6. **Polish & handoff** — descriptions are self-contained and copy-pasteable; no contradictions with the intake decisions.
